title: Performance Gaps Between Open-Loop, Certainty-Equivalent, and Optimal Control Under Action-Dependent Observations
abstract: arXiv:2610.33412v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In dynamical systems, feedback can improve performance by allowing decisions to depend on past observations, rather than being designed a priori. Under full observation, the current state is sufficient for decision-making; under partial observation, the controller must instead estimate the state from measurements. When actions also affect observations, control can have a dual role: actions influence both the state and the information available for future decisions. This interaction can invalidate certainty-equivalent (CE) control, a widely used strategy that applies state feedback policies as if the estimated state were the true state. We ask when this suboptimality leads to a quantitative performance gap that grows with the horizon. We study this question in a linear-quadratic system with bilinear observations by comparing the optimal policy, certainty-equivalent control, and the optimal open-loop (OL) policy. translated_title: 动作相关观测下开环控制、确定性等价控制与最优控制之间的性能差距
translated_abstract: 在动态系统中，反馈可以通过让决策依赖于过去的观测（而非先验设计）来提升性能。在完全观测下，当前状态足以支持决策；而在部分观测下，控制器必须从量测中估计状态。当动作还会影响观测时，控制便具有双重角色：动作既影响状态，也影响未来决策可获取的信息。这种交互作用可能使确定性等价（CE）控制失效——这是一种被广泛采用的策略，它将估计出的状态当作真实状态来执行状态反馈策略。我们探讨这种次优性何时会导致随时间范围增长的定量性能差距。我们在具有双线性观测的线性二次系统中研究这一问题，通过比较最优策略、确定性等价控制与最优开环（OL）策略来展开分析。我们识别出一种与具体实例相关……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文在动作会影响观测的线性二次系统中，比较最优策略、确定性等价控制与最优开环策略，刻画了确定性等价控制的次优性何时会产生随时间范围增长的定量性能差距。
en_tdlr: This paper compares optimal, certainty-equivalent, and optimal open-loop policies in linear-quadratic systems where actions affect observations, characterizing when the suboptimality of certainty-equivalent control leads to a quantitative performance gap that grows with the horizon.
